candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Find a least common (or target) denominator and rewrite one or both fractions as equivalent fractions with that common denominator to enable subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the same operation: determining an LCD/LCM (or target denominator) and converting fractions to equivalent forms with a shared denominator prior to subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference once quantities are in compatible form (e.g., like denominators or aligned whole/fraction parts) by subtracting appropriate parts and combining the result when no regrouping is the key step.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S02, B:S02, and C:S02 all focus on performing the subtraction itself after representations are compatible (typically subtract numerators with like denominators; C also mentions subtracting whole and fractional parts separately when borrowing is not needed).

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite mixed numbers or whole numbers into an equivalent form suitable for subtraction (e.g., mixed to improper, interpret nonstandard mixed numbers, or express a whole number with a fractional part/denominator).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S03 and B:S03 align tightly on converting mixed↔improper and rewriting whole numbers to match a needed denominator/structure. C:S03 bundles these same rewriting actions together with simplification; it is mapped here as the closest overall match, with simplification aspects noted as part of C’s broader framing.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: When a mixed-number subtraction would produce a negative fractional part, borrow 1 from the whole part and add one whole (d/d) to the fractional part, then continue the subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include the same regrouping/borrowing mechanism: decrease the whole part by 1 and add a full fraction (d/d) to make the fractional subtraction nonnegative before proceeding.

alignment_summary: Across the three codebooks, the skills align into four shared concepts with full (3/3) consensus: (1) converting to a common denominator, (2) performing subtraction once forms are compatible, (3) rewriting mixed/whole numbers into subtractable forms, and (4) borrowing/regrouping when the fractional part would be negative. Expert C’s S03 is broader (includes simplification) but still maps best to the shared rewriting concept given the available skill set.
